title: Defend Any Technical Project
interviewAnswer: Explain projects as problem → constraints → approach → your contribution → evaluation → result → limitations → what you would improve. Interviewers often care more about why you made a choice than the final architecture.
keyPoints: Know every metric on your CV
State limitations before the interviewer discovers them
Be ready to productionize the prototype
why: Most technical interviews spend more time probing projects than asking textbook definitions. A strong project answer proves ownership, reasoning, measurement and learning.
intuition: Treat every project like a compact engineering story: problem → constraints → approach → your contribution → validation → result → limitations → what you would change.
deepDive: Start from the real problem, not the model name. Separate what existed before you joined from what you personally changed. Explain why the selected architecture fit the data and constraints, name the metric and how it was measured, and volunteer one limitation before the interviewer finds it. Be able to zoom from a 60-second overview to implementation detail, productionization and alternative approaches.
workedExample: Instead of “I used CycleGAN,” say: “We needed high-resolution 3D reconstruction without paired CT/SEM data. An existing CycleGAN pipeline handled unpaired translation; my contribution was improving the interpolation/refinement and final multi-plane fusion.”
commonMistakes: Speaking only in “we” so ownership is unclear.
Listing technologies before explaining the problem.
Quoting a metric without knowing its definition or evaluation set.
followUps: What failed and what would you change today?
production: For each portfolio or work project, prepare an architecture diagram, exact inputs/outputs, dependencies, bottlenecks, deployment option, monitoring plan and one honest limitation.
